about: GLM-5.3-Flash EXL3 3.05bpw on one RTX 3090 inside 16 GiB of host RAM: routed experts streamed with O_DIRECT from a packed NVMe store through a ~960-expert pinned RAM tier and an elastic GPU expert cache, AVX2 CPU lane for cold RAM-resident decode picks (glm-flash-lite 0bd10f3 = v4.6.1-nvme, GLM53_MODE=nvme; the entrypoint applies its small-host budget below a 24 GiB cap)
setup: NEEDS: 1x RTX 3090 24 GB (expert cache capped at 1,376 slots by GLM53_EC_MAX_SLOTS so a desktop on the same GPU cannot run the CUDA graphs out of memory); the container is capped at 16 GiB of host RAM (resources: --memory 16g --memory-swap 16g, swap off inside the cap) and runs with --ulimit memlock=-1 (the RAM tier is cudaHostRegister'ed). Below a 24 GiB cap the image's entrypoint (v4.2-nvme) applies a small-host budget: -rcs 1 (exllamav3 host recurrent-state cache 1 GiB instead of 4), GLM53_NV_MARGIN_GB=1.5, GLM53_NV_PF_RING=128 prefill read-ahead slots, and a deeper NVMe reader pool (GLM53_NV_THREADS=48 x GLM53_NV_PIECE_KB=1024), each overridable; NVMe modes are refused only under 15 GiB. The RAM tier sizes itself from the cap (970 experts = 8.5 GiB on the measured box); measured 13.6 GiB at ready and a 14.6 GiB memory.peak while serving on v4.4. An x86-64 CPU with AVX2+FMA+F16C and >= 40 logical CPUs: nv2 pins its threads to the measured layout (CPU lane 2-23, main thread 24, controller 25, NVMe readers 26-39) when the container's CPUs hold it, else derives the layout from the container's CPU set and logs it. Disk: the 125.3 GB checkpoint (only its non-expert weights are read) plus the 117.3 GB packed expert store on a local NVMe filesystem that supports O_DIRECT (xfs, ext4). This launch is NVMe-bound: ~82 NVMe records per token at C1 (vs ~22 at 55 GB), read at 19.9 GB/s during C1 decode (76% of a 4x Samsung 9100 PRO md RAID0 xfs array, ~170k IOPS); a single drive or a slower array decodes proportionally slower. PREPARE (once, CPU only): the image's `pack-store` packs the routed experts (42 layers x 288 x 9.44 MB) from the read-only checkpoint into /nvx/glm53_flash_exl3_3.05bpw_experts.bin + .json, re-reads every record with O_DIRECT and checks its sha256, and byte-compares a sample against the checkpoint; `verify-store` repeats the sha256 re-read. Serving mounts /nvx read-only. MEASURED (image smoke of v4.2-nvme, the same serving code; v4.3-nvme smoke: 8k prefill 650, C1 13.03; HOM-272 N129, EPYC 7443P, PCIe 4.0 x16, natural completions, NVMe reads uncapped): 8k prefill 654 tok/s, decode C1 12.72 tok/s; the same digest at a 55 GiB cap: 8k prefill 662, C1 17.25. QUALITY: same kernels as the 55 GB launch: prefill / teacher-forced panel exact (top-1 1.0000, KL 0); decode not exact (AVX2 CPU lane on RAM-resident picks; paired decode KL 0.005 measured at 55 GB). Text only; OpenAI tool calls parsed from GLM's <tool_call> format. IMAGE v4.6.1-nvme (glm-flash-lite 0bd10f3): v4.6-nvme plus the fix for a decode-lookahead stall after the first max_rq_tokens requeue (glm-flash-lite #18); GLM53_MODE=nvme defaults to the N135 CPU-lane forward and the N136 decode switches (each settable to 0). MEASURED on v4.6-nvme at 16 GiB (HOM-272 N129, same session as a v4.4 control at 12.89): 8k prefill 650, decode C1 14.38 tok/s.
